digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verify gate and Pandoc integration testing
propositions: Complete live-Pandoc corpus replay contributes a measured 184.32-second macOS lower bound on every Gerrit Verify run, requiring removal from the per-change hot path while retaining complete real replay elsewhere.

Deterministic committed artifacts covering all Pandoc-bound inputs must be generated once via scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py and consumed by a fail-closed static converter during routine Verify, reducing subprocess work from 42s to 4s (90.8%) on the focused corpus phase.

One representative live product-path body per code_arrow, table, and prose stratum must remain in Gerrit Verify to retain version, platform-fingerprint, argv, stdin, timeout, and non-vacuous-dispatch probes against real Pandoc.

A dedicated external pandoc-corpus-replay job in .github/workflows/external-integration.yml must run the complete corpus through real Pandoc on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest weekly and on workflow_dispatch, proving all 178 bodies and 1,383 ordered settling conversions remain valid.
Every existing corpus assertion class, supported Python cell, supported operating system, and contractual Pandoc 3.6.1 behavior must remain present and functional across all verification modes.
Fixture regeneration must be deterministic and validated via a non-writing check path; platform-binary fingerprint and Pandoc version mismatches must fail before committed outputs are trusted.
